tickets.title: Third Avenue L stop closure pilot proposal
tickets.summary: A public speaker who rides the L train said the Third Avenue stop serves only about 5% of riders and is not a transfer or wheelchair-accessible station. He said closing it would save New Yorkers about 1,800 hours a day based on his simulation of MTA trip data. Action: The board should refer the proposal to the transportation committee and ask the MTA about a pilot closure of the Third Avenue stop.

tickets.title: 11th Street bike storage and delivery worker conditions
tickets.requester: Keith Powers (State Assembly Member); public speaker (unnamed); District Manager (unnamed)
tickets.summary: Over 100 electric delivery bikes are stored on the sidewalk and street at 11th Street and 1st Avenue, blocking businesses and creating a fire-hazard concern. Speakers and the district manager said the delivery workers have no legal parking or rest space, and that the district manager has worked on the issue since February 2024. The police plan an enforcement action on October 7 that would confiscate unparked bikes, and speakers asked for multilingual warnings and a tagging alternative. Action: The district office should coordinate with the precinct, sanitation, and the workers' groups on the enforcement plan, multilingual notice, and possible sites for bike parking, and report back to the board.

tickets.title: Drug activity and lighting in Seward Park
tickets.requester: Board member (unnamed); Parks, waterfront, and resiliency committee chair (unnamed)
tickets.summary: Residents and park groups reported increased drug use, homelessness, and dark spots in Seward Park. The Lower East Side Ecology Center, located in the park, said it is next to a restroom frequented by drug users. Police and outreach providers are active, and a speaker asked whether mobile crisis teams could be expanded to respond to drug-related emergencies instead of police. Action: The district office should ask the precinct, Parks, and DOT to fix dark lights in the park and to report on whether mobile crisis teams can be expanded to Seward Park.

tickets.title: Public restroom pilot locations in district
tickets.summary: The city is installing 17 free public restrooms as a one-year pilot, and two are planned for the district, including one near Delancey Plaza and one at Cooper Square and East Sixth Street. DOT is leading installation, which is expected in mid-October, and the committee raised concerns about access rules and emergency calls. Action: The board will vote next month on a resolution setting out what the board wants during the restroom pilot.

tickets.title: Essex Market RFP postponement and community input
tickets.summary: The land use and economic development committees passed two resolutions asking that the Essex Market RFP be shaped to keep the market community-run. EDC was not prepared to say whether the resolutions were included, and the RFP was due to go out at the end of the month. Action: The land use committee will meet with EDC this week and the board should press EDC to postpone issuing the RFP until the resolution requests are addressed.

tickets.title: Canal Street redesign update request
tickets.summary: The transportation committee sent a letter to the mayor and DOT that asked for an update on the Canal Street redesign project. The committee had received no update since January. Action: The district office should follow up with DOT for a Canal Street redesign update and report back to the board.

tickets.title: Manhattan Bridge exit safety concerns
tickets.summary: The transportation committee and a board member sent a letter to the mayor and DOT restating community concerns about the Manhattan Bridge exits at the foot of the bridge. The letter followed a recent crash and death and builds on resolutions passed over the past year and a half. Action: The board should track the mayor's and DOT's response to the letter and push for a plan to address the bridge exit concerns.

tickets.title: Congestion pricing impact on FDR Drive reporting
tickets.summary: A board member asked whether the congestion pricing impacts predicted for the FDR Drive in the air quality report actually occurred. The board had passed a resolution on those potential impacts about a year earlier. Action: The district office should ask MTA or DOT whether they will report on FDR congestion after congestion pricing, and request that report if none is planned.

tickets.title: 11 Allen Street full liquor license denial pending SLA
tickets.requester: Michelle Cooper Smith (SLA committee member); Carlin Chan (public speaker)
tickets.summary: The SLA committee voted 3 to 2 on a compromise to recommend a limited license for a new location at 11 Allen Street, and a board member moved for a straight denial. The community board voted 20 yes, 10 no, and 9 abstaining to deny, but without stipulations the State Liquor Authority could approve the license with the original requests. Speakers said the nearby Time Cafe has ignored its stipulations and draws large crowds outside. Action: The community board office should organize community members to attend the SLA hearing and support the denial recommendation.

tickets.title: Corrections to August SLA resolutions
tickets.summary: The SLA committee chair reported two clerical errors in the August resolutions. Item 10, Soft Hours Tea House, should have recommended denial of a beer and wine license, and item 3, Cozy Cafe, should have recommended denial of a beer and wine license instead of a full on-premises license. Action: None; the corrections were announced to the board and recorded.

tickets.title: Second vice chair special election result
tickets.summary: The board held a special election to fill the vacant second vice chair seat after Andrea stepped down. Daniel Tano received 25 votes and Zachary Thomas received 14 votes. Action: None; the board elected Daniel Tano as second vice chair.

tickets.title: Attendance and removal bylaws revision
tickets.summary: Proposed bylaw changes would send members who miss too many meetings a letter and ask them to meet with the executive committee before any removal process. The changes would also take attendance out of the removal process and require public members to follow conflict-of-interest policies. A question was raised about the executive committee's role in removal recommendations, and the bylaws require 28-day notice. Action: The board will vote on the bylaw changes at the October full board meeting after email circulation.

tickets.title: Board training requests on SLA and Robert's Rules
tickets.summary: The board chair announced new trainings on SLA procedures, Robert's Rules, and office procedures, but no dates have been set. The chair asked members to email requests for specific training topics. Action: The board chair will report training dates to the board and collect training topic requests by email.

tickets.title: Annual district needs and budget priorities vote
tickets.summary: The district manager said the board will vote in October on district needs and ranked expense and capital budget priorities for city agencies. District managers are meeting with over 20 agencies in September and early October to learn about cuts and vacancies. The draft housing plan's 7,000 units were 75% market rate, which conflicts with the board's top priority of affordable housing. Action: Committees should develop their budget priorities and the board should vote on district needs and ranked priorities in October.

tickets.title: City draft housing plan comments and engagement
tickets.summary: The city released a draft housing plan with a short comment window, so the board could comment only on existing positions. A board member asked whether there will be ongoing opportunities for community input on the housing plan. The district manager said committees should take positions proactively because public notice periods are shrinking. Action: Land use committee should take proactive positions on the housing plan and monitor future city engagement opportunities.

tickets.title: Mobile voting option for CEC elections resolution
tickets.requester: Health and Human Services committee chair (unnamed)
tickets.summary: The HHS committee presented a resolution urging NYC public schools to pilot a mobile-first voting option for community education council elections. Turnout has been about 2% because parents lack computers or have account problems. Speakers asked for clear messaging that immigration information is not collected and that eligibility is based on having a child in school. Action: The board should vote on the resolution and send it to the Department of Education's family and community empowerment office urging the mobile voting pilot and outreach.

tickets.title: Food and communication access for NYCHA residents
tickets.summary: A public speaker described long-term hardship for NYCHA residents, including lack of food, water, necessities, and work. He is hard of hearing and said communication access is essential for deaf and hard-of-hearing residents. Action: The district office should follow up with the relevant agencies on food and necessities support for NYCHA residents and on communication access for deaf residents.

tickets.title: East River Pier roller skating venue proposal
tickets.location_raw: East River Pier across from the Katherine Slip Mall
tickets.summary: A public speaker proposed a 300,000-square-foot multi-use indoor roller skating facility on an East River pier. The proposal would charge $8 admission and claims 250 to 500 jobs. Action: The board should refer the pier proposal to the land use committee for review and consideration.
